</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000813" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy"><p id="xdx_84D_eus-gaap--ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy_zYDiPMVKN61g" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_868_zLQeLXQoIMb9">Stock-Based
Compensation</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company measures all equity-based payment arrangements to employees, directors, and non-employee consultants in accordance with ASC
718, <i>Compensation - Stock Compensation</i>. The grant-date fair value of stock-based awards is determined using either the quoted
market price of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock or the Black-Scholes option valuation model, as appropriate for the instrument
type.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"></p>

<ix:exclude><!-- Field: Page; Sequence: 84; Value: 1 -->
    <div style="border-bottom: Black 1pt solid; margin-bottom: 6pt"><table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 10pt"><tr style="vertical-align: top; text-align: left"><td style="text-align: center; width: 100%">F-<!-- Field: Sequence; Type: Arabic; Name: PageNo -->11<!-- Field: /Sequence --></td></tr></table></div>
    <div style="break-before: page; margin-top: 6pt"><p style="margin: 0pt">&#160;</p></div>
    <!-- Field: /Page --></ix:exclude>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Compensation
cost for service-based awards is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period. For performance-based awards,
compensation cost is recognized when it becomes probable that the performance condition will be achieved. Forfeitures are recognized
as they occur.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
non-employee awards settled in equity including Series B Convertible Preferred Stock and warrants issued to consultants, the Company measures
the fair value at the grant date and recognizes the cost over the service period. Where awards are partially vested at issuance, the
vested fair value is recorded as a prepaid asset and amortized to expense over the remaining service period.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Black-Scholes option model incorporates the following assumptions: expected term (using the simplified method as the average of contractual
term and vesting period); expected stock price volatility (based on the Company&#8217;s historical stock price); risk-free interest rate
(based on U.S. Treasury rates for maturities approximating expected lives); and expected dividend yield of zero (as the Company has not
paid dividends and does not anticipate doing so in the foreseeable future). Changes in assumptions used to estimate fair value could
result in materially different results.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000815" name="us-gaap:DebtPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_846_eus-gaap--DebtPolicyTextBlock_zlP3XJdO424f" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_86B_zW2EUeZ9l7jl">Convertible
Debt and Original Issue Discount</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company accounts for convertible debt instruments under ASC 470-20, <i>Debt with Conversion and Other Options</i>. Debt issuance costs
and original issue discounts are recorded as a direct reduction to the carrying amount of the related debt instrument and amortized to
interest expense over the contractual term using the effective interest method in accordance with ASC 835-30.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000817" name="SHFS:WarrantLiabilitiesAndDerivativeInstrumentsPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_843_ecustom--WarrantLiabilitiesAndDerivativeInstrumentsPolicyTextBlock_zbrtV6A6F1C8" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_861_zgTvDGkPJym4">Warrant
Liabilities and Derivative Instruments</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company evaluates all financial instruments, including warrants and conversion features, at issuance to determine whether they
should be classified as equity or liabilities under ASC 815-40, <i>Derivatives and Hedging - Contracts in an Entity&#8217;s
Own Equity</i>, and ASC 480, <i>Distinguishing Liabilities from Equity</i>.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Warrants
that do not meet the criteria for equity classification are recorded as liabilities at fair value on the date of issuance. These warrant
liabilities are remeasured at fair value at each subsequent reporting date, with changes in fair value recognized in the consolidated
statements of operations. Warrants are valued using the Black-Scholes-Merton model.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000819" name="SHFS:PreferredStockClassificationAndMeasurementPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_84B_ecustom--PreferredStockClassificationAndMeasurementPolicyTextBlock_zDAg7RU3D70k" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_866_zJQXMQVXGIWc">Preferred
Stock - Classification and Measurement</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company evaluates preferred stock instruments under ASC 480 and ASC 815-40 to determine the appropriate classification between liabilities,
mezzanine equity, and permanent equity. </span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000821" name="SHFS:ExtinguishmentOfLiabilitiesPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_84C_ecustom--ExtinguishmentOfLiabilitiesPolicyTextBlock_zdNDowROaOJ9" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_86F_z8DJmpxZS0Cf">Extinguishment
of Liabilities</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">When
a financial liability is extinguished through the issuance of equity instruments, the Company accounts for the transaction under ASC
405-20, <i>Liabilities - Extinguishments of Liabilities</i>, and ASC 470-50, <i>Debt - Modifications and Extinguishments</i>.
The equity instruments issued are measured at fair value, and any difference between the carrying amount of the extinguished liability
and the fair value of the equity issued is recognized as a gain or loss on extinguishment in the consolidated statements of operations.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000823" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_849_eus-gaap--FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock_zcA5S5rZpKM8" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_86D_zoPT43hpA7P5">Fair
Value Measurements</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company utilizes the fair value hierarchy to apply fair value measurements. The fair value hierarchy is based on inputs to valuation
techniques that are used to measure fair values that are either observable or unobservable. Observable inputs reflect assumptions market
participants would use in pricing an asset or liability based on market data obtained from independent sources, while unobservable inputs
reflect a reporting entity&#8217;s pricing based upon its own market assumptions. The basis for fair value measurements for each level
within the hierarchy is described below:</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Level
1</b>:  Quoted prices for identical assets or liabilities in active markets.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Level
2</b>:  Quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets; quoted prices for identical or similar assets or liabilities
in markets that are not active; or model-derived valuations whose inputs are observable or whose significant value drivers are observable.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Level
3</b>:  Valuations derived from techniques in which one or more significant inputs are unobservable.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000825" name="us-gaap:SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_841_eus-gaap--SegmentReportingPolicyPolicyTextBlock_zDGd80XRqWp8" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_861_zBK84JUtyJti">Segment
Reporting</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company operates as <span id="xdx_90F_eus-gaap--NumberOfReportableSegments_dc_uInteger_c20250101__20251231_z7hNdW0gUR64" title="Number of reportable segments"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" id="Fact000827" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF" unitRef="Integer">one</ix:nonFraction></span>
reportable segment providing financial services and banking solutions to CRBs under ASC 280, <i>Segment Reporting</i>. The chief
operating decision maker, the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer, reviews financial information on a consolidated basis when
allocating resources and assessing performance.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000829" name="SHFS:FinancialAssetsMeasuredAtAmortizedCostPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_848_ecustom--FinancialAssetsMeasuredAtAmortizedCostPolicyTextBlock_zzJgqoduiUM4" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_865_zy2DUlUCuefd">Financial
Assets Measured at Amortized Cost</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">For
financial assets within the scope of ASC 326, the Company measures the allowance for credit losses based on relevant information about
past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts of future economic conditions that affect the collectability
of the reported amounts. The allowance is deducted from the amortized cost basis of the financial asset on the consolidated balance sheet,
and the net amount represents management&#8217;s best estimate of the cash flows expected to be collected. Changes in the allowance for credit
losses are recognized as credit loss expense or reversal in the consolidated statements of operations.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company considers the following factors, among others, in estimating expected credit losses:</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse">
  <tr style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></td>
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; width: 0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</span></td>
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Historical
    loss experience and default rates for instruments with similar risk characteristics;</span></td></tr>
  <tr style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></td>
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</span></td>
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The

  <tr style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></td>

    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Current
    and forecasted macroeconomic conditions over the reasonable and supportable forecast period, reverting to historical averages beyond
    that period; and</span></td></tr>
  <tr style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; vertical-align: top">
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></td>
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#9679;</span></td>
    <td style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Collateral
    arrangements, recourse provisions, and other credit enhancements.</span></td></tr>
  </table>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0 0 0 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Financial
assets are written off against the allowance when management determines that the asset is uncollectible and all reasonable collection
efforts have been exhausted. Subsequent recoveries, if any, are credited to the allowance for credit losses.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000831" name="SHFS:ContractAssetsPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_84B_ecustom--ContractAssetsPolicyTextBlock_zuAkadxh6nHa" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"><b><span id="xdx_869_zGzREkI3w4tg">Contract Asset</span></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: justify">The contract asset
recognized in connection with the Second Amended CAA with PCCU are not financial asset within the scope of ASC 326. This asset
represent costs incurred to fulfill the contract specifically, the cost of assuming the stand-ready guarantee obligation (ASC 460)
and the contingent indemnification exposure (ASC 326). The contract asset is amortized on a systematic and rational basis over the
contract term consistent with the release of the underlying guarantee exposure. Contract asset are evaluated for impairment under
ASC 340-40-35-2 when facts and circumstances indicate the carrying amount may not be recoverable; any impairment is recognized in
the period identified and may not be subsequently reversed.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0; margin-bottom: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000833" name="SHFS:StandReadyGuaranteesPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_847_ecustom--StandReadyGuaranteesPolicyTextBlock_zFnRHsrG7JQ" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Stand
Ready Guarantees &#8211; ASC 460</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company accounts for financial guarantees in accordance with ASC 460, <i>Guarantees</i>. At the inception of a guarantee, the Company
recognizes a liability equal to the fair value of the stand-ready obligation assumed. This non-contingent liability represents the value
of the obligation undertaken by the Company to stand ready to perform under the guarantee, irrespective of the likelihood that a payment
will actually be required.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Subsequent
to initial recognition, the stand-ready liability is amortized over the contractual term of the guarantee on a systematic basis that
reflects the Company&#8217;s release from risk. If, at any reporting date, a contingent loss accrual required under ASC 450, <i>Contingencies</i>,
exceeds the unamortized ASC 460 carrying amount, the Company records the higher contingent loss estimate in accordance with that guidance.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000835" name="us-gaap:CreditLossFinancialInstrumentPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_840_eus-gaap--CreditLossFinancialInstrumentPolicyTextBlock_zOQQqBdKtQkd" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_86A_zhzOBMS6RvQ3">Financial Indemnification Liabilities</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Under
ASC 326-20, the Company recognizes a financial indemnification liability for its indemnification obligation to
PCCU under the Second Amended CAA. This liability represents the Company&#8217;s up to 65% share of the lifetime expected credit
losses on the covered CRB loan portfolio, measured on a probability-weighted basis and updated each reporting period to reflect
current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts of future economic conditions. The financial indemnification liability
methodology considers historical loss experience, borrower-specific credit quality, collateral values, and forward-looking economic
assumptions including conditions specific to the cannabis industry.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin: 0"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
financial indemnification liability is measured independently from, and recognized in addition to, the ASC 460 stand-ready guarantee liability. The two liabilities
coexist separately on the consolidated balance sheet and do not offset or true up to each other. The ASC 460 liability is fixed at inception
and released over the guarantee term, while the financial indemnification liability is dynamic and remeasured each quarter. Changes in the financial indemnification liability
are recognized as credit loss expense or credit loss income in the consolidated statements of operations in the period of remeasurement.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; text-align: justify; margin: 0"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"></span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000851" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock"><p id="xdx_841_eus-gaap--NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock_zXUqRTjTi6fb" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b><span id="xdx_86D_zmzCozPLk09d">Recently
Issued Accounting Standards</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Standards
Adopted in 2025</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>ASU
2023-09 - Income Taxes (Topic 740):</b> In December 2023, the FASB issued ASU 2023-09, which requires additional disaggregated
disclosures in the income tax rate reconciliation and disclosures of income taxes paid by jurisdiction. The standard is effective for
annual periods beginning after December 15, 2024. The Company adopted this standard prospectively as of January 1, 2025. Adoption did
not have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial statements. This is reported on a prospective basis.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>ASU
2024-02 - Codification Improvements:</b> In March 2024, the FASB issued ASU 2024-02, which removes references to the FASB Concepts
Statements from the Codification. The standard is effective for public entities for years beginning after December 15, 2024. The Company
adopted this standard prospectively as of January 1, 2025. Adoption did not have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial statements.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>ASU
2024-01 &#8211; Compensation - Stock Compensation (Topic 718): Profits Interest and Similar Awards:</b> In March 2024, the
FASB issued ASU 2024-01, which clarifies whether profits interest and similar awards are subject to ASC 718. The standard is
effective for years beginning after December 15, 2024. The Company adopted this standard prospectively as of January 1, 2025.
Adoption did not have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial statements.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Standards
Not Yet Adopted</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>ASU
2024-03 / ASU 2025-01 - Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses (Subtopic 220-40):</b> In November 2024, the FASB issued ASU
2024-03, subsequently clarified by ASU 2025-01 (January 2025), requiring entities to disaggregate certain income statement expense line
items in the footnotes, including purchases of inventory, employee compensation, depreciation, and amortization. The standard is effective
for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2026, and interim periods within annual periods beginning after December 15, 2027. Early
adoption is permitted. The Company plans to adopt prospectively and does not anticipate a material impact on its financial reporting.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>ASU
2024-04 &#8211; Debt - Debt with Conversion and Other Options (Subtopic 470-20): Induced Conversions:</b> In November 2024,
the FASB issued ASU 2024-04, which clarifies the accounting for induced conversions of convertible debt. The standard is effective
for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2025. The Company plans to adopt prospectively and does not anticipate a material
impact on its financial reporting.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>ASU
2025-05 - Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic 326): Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets:</b> In July 2025, the
FASB issued ASU 2025-05, which provides a practical expedient allowing entities to assume current credit conditions remain unchanged
for the remaining life of current accounts receivable and current contract assets under ASC 606. The standard is effective for years
beginning after December 15, 2025. The Company is currently evaluating the potential impact on its consolidated financial statements.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>ASU
2025-08 - Financial Instruments - Credit Losses (Topic 326): Purchased Loans:</b> In December 2025, the FASB issued ASU
2025-08, which expands the population of acquired financial assets subject to the gross-up approach for recognizing credit losses at
acquisition. The standard introduces the concept of &#8220;purchased seasoned loans&#8221; and requires acquired loans (other than
credit cards) that have not experienced significant credit deterioration since origination to follow the gross-up approach. The
amendments are effective for annual periods beginning after December 15, 2026. Due to the Company&#8217;s Second Amended CAA with
PCCU, management believes this standard may have a material impact on the Company&#8217;s financial statements upon adoption. The
Company is currently evaluating the scope and magnitude of that impact.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company will continue to monitor the development of accounting standards and intends to adopt them in accordance with their respective
effective dates. Additional disclosures will be provided in future filings as the Company completes its assessment.</span></p>

The Company issued <span id="xdx_90D_eus-gaap--CommonStockSharesIssued_iI_c20251003_ztwjvMSrJv27"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesIssued" contextRef="AsOf2025-10-03" id="Fact000866" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">37,517</ix:nonFraction></span> unregistered

<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000934" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsDisclosureTextBlock"><p id="xdx_806_eus-gaap--GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsDisclosureTextBlock_zJP3pjZY5C1f" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Note
4 - <span id="xdx_82F_z1nCYxBCPohh">Goodwill and Finite-lived Intangible Assets</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: left; text-indent: -37pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>2024
Impairment</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: -37pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of December 31, 2024, the Company recorded full impairment charges against all remaining goodwill and finite-lived intangible assets,
which were derived primarily from the October 2022 acquisition of Abaca. The impairment charges
totaled $<span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived_pn5n6_c20240101__20241231_z8oaUCF5mY74" title="Impairment charges"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived" contextRef="From2024-01-012024-12-31" id="Fact000936" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">3.1</ix:nonFraction></span> million, comprised of $<span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived_pn4n6_c20240101__20241231__us-gaap--FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis__us-gaap--MarketingRelatedIntangibleAssetsMember_zu2fiyjswQb4" title="Impairment charges"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived" contextRef="From2024-01-012024-12-31_us-gaap_MarketingRelatedIntangibleAssetsMember" id="Fact000938" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-4" scale="6" unitRef="USD">0.05</ix:nonFraction></span> million for market-related intangible assets, $<span id="xdx_901_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived_pn4n6_c20240101__20241231__us-gaap--FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis__us-gaap--CustomerRelationshipsMember_zmnC51KxPNV8" title="Impairment charges"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived" contextRef="From2024-01-012024-12-31_us-gaap_CustomerRelationshipsMember" id="Fact000940" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-4" scale="6" unitRef="USD">0.05</ix:nonFraction></span> million for customer relationships, and
$<span id="xdx_90F_eus-gaap--ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived_pn5n6_c20240101__20241231__us-gaap--FiniteLivedIntangibleAssetsByMajorClassAxis__us-gaap--DevelopedTechnologyRightsMember_znkA6dVKbc68" title="Impairment charges"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ImpairmentOfIntangibleAssetsFinitelived" contextRef="From2024-01-012024-12-31_us-gaap_DevelopedTechnologyRightsMember" id="Fact000942" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">3.0</ix:nonFraction></span> million for developed technology. Impairment expense for the year ended December 31, 2024 was $<span id="xdx_909_eus-gaap--AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets_pn5n6_c20240101__20241231_zMqLoksdWuNj" title="Impairment expense"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:AmortizationOfIntangibleAssets" contextRef="From2024-01-012024-12-31" id="Fact000944" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">6.1</ix:nonFraction></span> million. Following these
charges, the carrying values of all such assets were zero as of December 31, 2024.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left; text-indent: -0.25pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>420
IT Asset Acquisition </b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">In
December 2025, the Company&#8217;s wholly-owned subsidiary, Safe Harbor Managed Services LLC, completed an asset acquisition from
LBMW LLC, doing business as 420 IT Solutions (&#8220;420 IT Solutions&#8221;), a managed services business. The purchased assets
consist primarily of intellectual property, including a registered trademark, and certain assigned customer contracts and goodwill.
No cash consideration was paid. The aggregate purchase price consisted of <span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesAcquisitions_c20250101__20251231__us-gaap--StatementEquityComponentsAxis__us-gaap--CommonStockMember_zkJfufOpWrpl" title="Aggregate purchase price"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:StockIssuedDuringPeriodSharesAcquisitions" contextRef="From2025-01-012025-12-31_us-gaap_CommonStockMember" id="Fact000946" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">125,000</ix:nonFraction></span>
shares of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock (the &#8220;Earnout Shares&#8221;), which vest based on the achievement of net
revenue performance targets during the periods ending December 31, 2026 and December 31, 2027, and the assumption of certain
specified liabilities.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
transaction was accounted for as an asset acquisition under ASC 805-50. The total consideration transferred was measured at the fair
value of the Earnout Shares at the acquisition date. Because vesting is contingent solely on future performance conditions, the
Earnout Shares are accounted for as contingent consideration and recognized as the performance conditions become probable of
achievement. Therefore, the Company did not record any intangible assets and contingent liability as of December 31, 2025. If
circumstances change when the revenue target is probable, then the intangible assets and a contingent liability will be
recorded within one year from the acquisition date.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.25pt"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000948" name="us-gaap:LoansNotesTradeAndOtherReceivablesDisclosureTextBlock"><p id="xdx_80B_eus-gaap--LoansNotesTradeAndOtherReceivablesDisclosureTextBlock_zq0Vq1l8jWOf" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: left; text-indent: -0.5in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Note
5 - <span id="xdx_820_zwrKZC2k2jnf">Loans Receivable</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: justify; text-indent: -0.5in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">As
of December 31, 2024, the Company held one commercial real estate loan receivable with a gross carrying value of $<span id="xdx_90F_eus-gaap--NotesReceivableGross_iI_pn5n6_c20241231__us-gaap--DebtInstrumentAxis__custom--CommercialRealEstateLoansReceivableMember_z1cGDdOQXqd5" title="Commercial real estate loans receivable, gross"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableGross" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-31_custom_CommercialRealEstateLoansReceivableMember" id="Fact000950" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">0.4</ix:nonFraction></span>
million, net of no allowance for credit losses. On July 31, 2025, the Company sold this loan to PCCU, a related party to improve
liquidity. </ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact000979" name="us-gaap:InvestmentTextBlock"><p id="xdx_80B_eus-gaap--InvestmentTextBlock_zzgrwikNEpQa" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Note
6 - <span id="xdx_823_zeadNCgnOI4g">Investment in Preferred Securities</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">On
September 30, 2025, as partial consideration received in connection with the issuance of <span id="xdx_908_eus-gaap--PreferredStockSharesIssued_iI_c20250930__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--SeriesBWarrantsMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AditxtIncMember_zSMAwIHOZCTj" title="Preferred stock, shares issued"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:PreferredStockSharesIssued" contextRef="AsOf2025-09-30_custom_SeriesBWarrantsMember_custom_AditxtIncMember" id="Fact000981" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="Shares">1,875</ix:nonFraction></span> shares of Series B Convertible Preferred
Stock and Series B Warrants to purchase Common Stock (see Note 19), the Company received preferred shares of Aditxt, Inc. (&#8220;ADTX&#8221;),
a publicly traded company. The Series B Convertible Preferred Stock was issued at $<span id="xdx_90E_eus-gaap--PreferredStockParOrStatedValuePerShare_iI_pid_c20250930__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--SeriesBConvertiblePreferredStockMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AditxtIncMember_zjYDKebKICul" title="Preferred stock, par value"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:PreferredStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" contextRef="AsOf2025-09-30_custom_SeriesBConvertiblePreferredStockMember_custom_AditxtIncMember" id="Fact000983" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="USDPShares">800</ix:nonFraction></span> per share. No cash was exchanged in this transaction.
The ADTX preferred securities had an estimated fair value and carrying value of $<span id="xdx_90E_eus-gaap--ProceedsFromIssuanceOfConvertiblePreferredStock_pn5n6_c20250930__20250930__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--SeriesBConvertiblePreferredStockMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AditxtIncMember_z5R4BZielsHc" title="Proceeds from issuance of convertible preferred stock"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromIssuanceOfConvertiblePreferredStock" contextRef="From2025-09-302025-09-30_custom_SeriesBConvertiblePreferredStockMember_custom_AditxtIncMember" id="Fact000985" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">1.5</ix:nonFraction></span> million at the date of receipt.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><span id="xdx_904_eus-gaap--PreferredStockVotingRights_c20250930__20250930__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--SeriesBConvertiblePreferredStockMember__dei--LegalEntityAxis__custom--AditxtIncMember_zhKc8hypuZj" title="Voting rights"><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-09-302025-09-30_custom_SeriesBConvertiblePreferredStockMember_custom_AditxtIncMember" id="Fact000987" name="us-gaap:PreferredStockVotingRights">The
investment represents less than 20% of the voting interests in ADTX, and the Company does not have the ability to exercise significant
influence or control over ADTX.</ix:nonNumeric></span> Accordingly, the investment is accounted for under ASC 321, <i>Investments &#8211; Equity Securities</i>.
Because ADTX&#8217;s preferred shares are not actively traded and lack a readily determinable fair value, the Company has elected to
measure the investment at cost, less any impairment, adjusted for observable price changes in orderly transactions for identical or similar
instruments, as permitted under ASC 321-10-35-2.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">During

shares of its preferred stock held by the Company pursuant to the preferred share terms, resulting in cash proceeds of $<span id="xdx_901_ecustom--ProceedsFromSaleOfPreferredSecurities_pn4n6_c20250101__20251231_zqk4c5n7JJSl" title="Proceeds from sale of preferred securities"><ix:nonFraction name="SHFS:ProceedsFromSaleOfPreferredSecurities" contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" id="Fact000991" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-4" scale="6" unitRef="USD">0.05</ix:nonFraction></span>
million. No gain or loss was recognized on this redemption. No impairments or other observable price adjustments were recognized during the

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001051" name="SHFS:LoanPortfolioIndemnificationObligationsTextBlock"><p id="xdx_80E_ecustom--LoanPortfolioIndemnificationObligationsTextBlock_zb8pCUOhIAyi" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: left"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Note
8 - <span id="xdx_826_zmZRbpof26R5">Loan Portfolio Indemnification Obligations</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: center">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Under the Second Amended CAA, the
Company indemnifies PCCU for up to 65% of Default-Related Losses on PCCU&#8217;s CRB loan portfolio. The Agreement has a stated
effective date of October 1, 2025. The Company, and PCCU reached agreement on the material economic terms of the Second Amended CAA on or about October
1, 2025, following completion of the September 2025 Recapitalization. The written agreement was formally executed on February 4, 2026;
the intervening period involved only procedural and documentation matters that did not affect the substance of the agreed terms. Accordingly,
the Company has given effect to the Second Amended CAA from October 1, 2025, consistent with ASC 606 contract modification guidance.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The obligation is recognized as two independent,
coexisting liabilities that do not offset each other: (i) a noncontingent stand-ready guarantee liability under ASC 460, measured at
fair value at inception, and (ii) a contingent expected credit loss liability under ASC 326-20, representing the Company&#8217;s up to
65% share of estimated lifetime expected credit losses on the PCCU CRB portfolio. Each liability is recognized with a corresponding contract
asset under ASC 340-40-25-2, as the indemnification costs are directly related to the Agreement and are expected to be recovered through
the Company&#8217;s up to 65% share of loan program income. The net Day 1 equity impact is zero.</p>


<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><p id="xdx_8A5_zJ1Wni1oCg1l" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b><i>ASC 460 - Guarantee
Liability</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The issuance of a guarantee imposes a noncontingent
obligation to stand ready to perform; initial recognition is required at inception regardless of whether payment is probable. The stand-ready
liability is recognized separately from the ASC 326 liability.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The stand-ready liability is measured at fair value
at inception under ASC 820-10 using a market-based insurance pricing approach, classified as Level 3 due to the absence of observable
market inputs for cannabis lending guarantees. The fair value of a guarantee at inception reflects the premium that a market participant
(analogized to a specialty insurance carrier) would charge in an arm&#8217;s-length transaction to underwrite the same risk. Because no
direct market comparable exist for cannabis CRB loan portfolio guarantees, management estimated the standalone selling price by constructing
the premium components a specialty financial guarantor would require. The fair value incorporates three components: (a) the expected loss
element, representing the probability-weighted losses the guarantor expects to absorb; (b) a stand-ready risk premium, representing the
additional compensation a market participant would require for uncertainty, volatility, and the uncapped nature of the commitment beyond
expected losses; and (c) a time value adjustment. Key Level 3 inputs are as follows:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

of Significant Unobservable Input</span></span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><p id="xdx_8A4_zKKHeuj89S7c" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The maximum potential number of future payments under
the guarantee is approximately $<span id="xdx_903_eus-gaap--GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure_iI_pn5n6_c20251231_zfH37NEtYIql" title="Maximum potential number of future payments"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:GuaranteeObligationsMaximumExposure" contextRef="AsOf2025-12-31" id="Fact001089" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">33.8</ix:nonFraction></span> million, representing <span id="xdx_900_eus-gaap--DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage_iI_pid_dp_c20251231__us-gaap--DebtInstrumentAxis__custom--CRBLoanMember_zdoGn0Ur66gh" title="Outstanding loan percentage"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:DebtInstrumentInterestRateStatedPercentage" contextRef="AsOf2025-12-31_custom_CRBLoanMember" id="Fact001091" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">65</ix:nonFraction></span>% of the total outstanding CRB loan portfolio balance. The indemnification
percentage is subject to reduction under the Agreement&#8217;s Listing-Related Adjustment Clause.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The stand-ready guarantee liability is reduced through amortization on a straight-line basis over three years, representing
the weighted average life of the underlying loan portfolio at inception. The release period and pattern are reassessed at least annually
and will be adjusted prospectively if material changes in portfolio composition, paydowns, or maturities indicate that the weighted average
life assumption is no longer appropriate. The corresponding contract asset is amortized on the same basis as operating expense partially offset
by the liability release to income each period.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b><i>ASC 326-20 - Financial Indemnification Liability</i></b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Financial indemnification liability
are estimated using a PD &#215; LGD framework segmented by PCCU&#8217;s internal risk rating scale. Management uses PCCU&#8217;s
reserve methodology as a baseline and independently evaluates key assumptions, with adjustments where management&#8217;s estimates
differ from PCCU&#8217;s. The cannabis industry specific risk is reflected through a 16.6% qualitative LGD premium and
management&#8217;s independent assessment of Tranche C.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001093" name="us-gaap:AllowanceForCreditLossesOnFinancingReceivablesTableTextBlock"><p id="xdx_898_eus-gaap--AllowanceForCreditLossesOnFinancingReceivablesTableTextBlock_zjqya7qAqIki" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The
indemnified portfolio is segmented into three tranches. Loans rated 9 or 10 are individually evaluated rather than included in the
pooled analysis:</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><p id="xdx_8A5_zKJHhw0jUZd4" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify"><b>&#160;</b></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">There is a single loan in Tranche C that is individually
evaluated due to its past-maturity status (original maturity July 2024) and commercial and industrial or C&amp;I structure secured solely by a UCC filing on business
assets with certain personal guarantees. Management applied a 35% PD and 50% LGD on the uncollateralized gap of approximately $<span id="xdx_907_eus-gaap--NotesReceivableGross_iI_pn5n6_c20251231__us-gaap--CollateralAxis__us-gaap--UncollateralizedMember_zN6rEc7XW3n5" title="Uncollateralized gap"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableGross" contextRef="AsOf2025-12-31_us-gaap_UncollateralizedMember" id="Fact001111" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">3.4</ix:nonFraction></span> million.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Loans in the portfolio are secured primarily by real
estate used for cannabis-specific purposes, including cultivation facilities, processing facilities, and retail dispensaries, and in certain
cases by business assets under UCC filings. Because cannabis-use properties have limited alternative-use marketability under current federal
law, management applies a two-step discount to collateral values: (i) elimination of the cannabis license premium (the &#8220;green tax&#8221;),
reflecting that a non-cannabis buyer would not ascribe value to the cannabis operating license embedded in the appraised value; and (ii)
a reduction to the remaining value to reflect proceeds realizable from a liquidation sale to a non-cannabis buyer. This methodology results
in adjusted portfolio collateral of approximately $<span id="xdx_901_ecustom--FinancingReceivableAdjustedPortfolioCollateral_iI_pn5n6_c20251231__us-gaap--AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis__us-gaap--FinanceReceivablesMember_zIKB3FmekaNl" title="Adjusted portfolio collateral"><ix:nonFraction name="SHFS:FinancingReceivableAdjustedPortfolioCollateral" contextRef="AsOf2025-12-31_us-gaap_FinanceReceivablesMember" id="Fact001113" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">44.1</ix:nonFraction></span> million against a gross balance of $<span id="xdx_900_eus-gaap--FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLosses_iI_pn5n6_c20251231__us-gaap--AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis__us-gaap--FinanceReceivablesMember_zGFGDzytvD41" title="Financing receivable gross balance"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivableAllowanceForCreditLosses" contextRef="AsOf2025-12-31_us-gaap_FinanceReceivablesMember" id="Fact001115" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">52.1</ix:nonFraction></span> million.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The portfolio has experienced zero credit losses since
program inception. Management supplements this limited loss history with cannabis industry benchmarks and peer data. Cannabis industry-specific
risk including 100% single-industry concentration, Schedule I federal status, and collateral marketability constraints is reflected through
an embedded 16.6% qualitative LGD premium across all pooled tranches.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">Expected credit losses are estimated using historical
loss rates derived from a five-year lookback period, reflecting 2 restructured loans out of 28 over that period. Management determined that
reasonable and supportable forecasts of future economic conditions beyond the historical loss experience could not be made for this portfolio,
given its limited loss history and the significant uncertainty surrounding the cannabis regulatory and legal environment. Accordingly,
the historical loss rates are applied without forward-looking adjustment, with immediate reversion to historical rates.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">The financial indemnification liability is remeasured quarterly; changes
are recognized as credit loss expense or income per ASC 326-20-35-8. The inception-date contract asset is reduced as underlying loans
pay down or mature and is not subject to straight-line amortization. The 65% indemnification percentage is subject to reduction under
the Agreement&#8217;s Listing-Related Adjustment Clause if the Company fails to maintain NASDAQ listing standards. A reduction would result
in a partial release of the ASC 460 liability to income, a downward remeasurement of the financial indemnification liability, and an impairment assessment
of the related contract assets.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">For the year ended December 31,
2025, the Company recognized a reversal of provision of $<span id="xdx_903_eus-gaap--LossContingencyLossInPeriod_pn5n6_c20250101__20251231__us-gaap--AccountsNotesLoansAndFinancingReceivableByReceivableTypeAxis__us-gaap--FinanceReceivablesMember_zcL06dCegWz4" title="Reversal of provision"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:LossContingencyLossInPeriod" contextRef="From2025-01-012025-12-31_us-gaap_FinanceReceivablesMember" id="Fact001117" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">0.2</ix:nonFraction></span>
million, representing the systematic release of the ASC 460 stand-ready guarantee liability computed over the
weighted-average remaining life of three years of the covered CRB loan portfolio. As of December 31, 2025, the Company did not
change its financial indemnification liability, as such there was no impact on the consolidated statements of operations.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">As of December 31, 2024, there was no financial indemnification liability
as the Company ceased indemnifying the loan portfolio subject to the first amendment to the PCCU CAA. As of December 31, 2024, the Company
favorably reversed a $<span id="xdx_90A_ecustom--IndemnificationLiability_iI_pn5n6_c20241231_zV0qofvA7ez2" title="Indemnification liability"><ix:nonFraction name="SHFS:IndemnificationLiability" contextRef="AsOf2024-12-31" id="Fact001119" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="-5" scale="6" unitRef="USD">1.4</ix:nonFraction></span>M indemnification liability. For the period between January 1, 2025 and September 30, 2025, the Company did not
indemnify loan portfolio.</p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 0; text-align: justify">&#160;</p>

</ix:nonNumeric><p id="xdx_8AB_zVfT1jdU9nug" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Account
fee income consists of fees earned from cannabis-related businesses maintaining accounts with the Company&#8217;s financial institution
partners, including deposit account fees, account activity fees, and onboarding income. These fees are recognized periodically in accordance
with the fee schedules established with financial institution partners. Account fee income also includes merchant income earned through
referral arrangements with third-party payment processors, under which the Company receives a percentage of net revenue generated by
referred merchants, recognized as earned. </span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Loan
program income represents the Company&#8217;s allocated share of interest earned on cannabis-related business loans originated by PCCU.
Under the First Amended Commercial Alliance Agreement, effective January 1, 2025, the Company&#8217;s share of loan program income is
determined by a loan yield allocation formula that incorporates the Constant Maturity U.S. Treasury Rate published by the Federal Reserve,
along with a proprietary risk rating formula to determine the allocation between the Company and PCCU. Loan program income is recognized
over the loan term as earned. </span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Investment
income represents the Company&#8217;s share of interest earned on net investable cannabis-related business deposit balances held at PCCU,
recognized monthly based on the average net daily deposit balance. Under the CAA, investment income was reduced by an investment
hosting fee paid to PCCU. Under the First Amended CAA, effective January 1, 2025, the hosting investment fee was eliminated and the Company
receives all investment income earned on CRB funds invested on its behalf by PCCU.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">Safe
Harbor Program income represents fees earned under the Company&#8217;s Master Program Agreement, which grants licensees a non-exclusive,
non-transferable right to implement and utilize the Safe Harbor Program. Revenue is recognized over the term of the agreement as the
performance obligation is satisfied.</span></p>
<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

</ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="From2025-01-01to2025-12-31" escape="true" id="Fact001268" name="us-gaap:RelatedPartyTransactionsDisclosureTextBlock"><p id="xdx_807_eus-gaap--RelatedPartyTransactionsDisclosureTextBlock_zeg8llRrPILe" style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: left; text-indent: -0.5in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Note
10 - <span id="xdx_82A_zfCiaP7kENnd">Related Party Transactions</span></b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0.5in; text-align: left; text-indent: -0.5in"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
Company identifies related parties in accordance with ASC 850 and Rule 1-02(u) of Regulation S-X.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>Partner
Colorado Credit Union (&#8220;PCCU&#8221;) - Related Party Status</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt"><b>&#160;</b></span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">PCCU
is a related party because it held approximately <span id="xdx_90A_ecustom--PercentageOfCommonStockHeld_c20250101__20251231__us-gaap--RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis__custom--PartnerColoradoCreditUnionMember_zbQfP79PSMag" title="Common stock held by related party"><ix:nonFraction name="SHFS:PercentageOfCommonStockHeld" contextRef="From2025-01-012025-12-31_custom_PartnerColoradoCreditUnionMember" id="Fact001270" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">25.2</ix:nonFraction>%</span> and <span id="xdx_907_ecustom--PercentageOfCommonStockHeld_c20240101__20241231__us-gaap--RelatedPartyTransactionsByRelatedPartyAxis__custom--PartnerColoradoCreditUnionMember_zV0wwX3wlG8l" title="Common stock held by related party"><ix:nonFraction name="SHFS:PercentageOfCommonStockHeld" contextRef="From2024-01-012024-12-31_custom_PartnerColoradoCreditUnionMember" id="Fact001272" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" scale="-2" unitRef="Pure">38.8</ix:nonFraction>%</span> of the Company&#8217;s Common Stock as of December 31, 2025 and 2024,
respectively. PCCU is also the largest holder of the Company&#8217;s Series B Convertible Preferred Stock (approximately 43% of outstanding
shares and associated warrants) and holds the majority of the Company&#8217;s cash deposits. These factors give PCCU the ability to significantly
influence the Company&#8217;s management and operating policies.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

This amended and restated
agreement allows for interest-only payments until January 5, 2027, postponing principal payments, with full repayment due by October

transaction was accounted for under ASC 470-50, Debt &#8211; Modifications and Extinguishments. The fair value of the Series B Convertible
Preferred Stock and Series B Warrants to purchase Common Stock issued was estimated at $<span id="xdx_90C_eus-gaap--PreferredStockNoParValue_iI_pid_c20250930__us-gaap--StatementClassOfStockAxis__custom--SeriesBConvertiblePreferredStockMember_zJ8zUCaWQLV" title="Preferred stock par values"><ix:nonFraction name="us-gaap:PreferredStockNoParValue" contextRef="AsOf2025-09-30_custom_SeriesBConvertiblePreferredStockMember" id="Fact001348" format="ixt:numdotdecimal" decimals="INF" unitRef="USDPShares">800</ix:nonFraction></span> per unit, which represented the cash

the Company did not recognize a gain (loss) on extinguishment of debt. As a result of the Debt Cancellation Agreement, there was no outstanding
balance on the Senior Secured Promissory Note as of December 31, 2025.</span></p>

September 30, 2025, prior to their maturity date, the Notes were exchanged for Series B Convertible Preferred Stock and Series B

per unit, the same price paid by unaffiliated third-party investors for identical instruments on the same date.</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">&#160;</span></p>

<p style="font: 10pt Times New Roman, Times, Serif; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; margin-left: 0; text-align: justify"><span style="font-family: Times New Roman, Times, Serif; font-size: 10pt">The
